questions.question_text:
The daily profit, in dollars, from selling $x$ items is $P(x) = 180x - 3x^{2}$, for $0 \le x \le 50$.
How many items should be sold to maximise the profit?

options.why: Differentiated $3x^{2}$ as $3x$, then solved $180 - 3x = 0$.
Took the right endpoint of the domain without testing the stationary point.

questions.solution_text:
$P'(x) = 180 - 6x$
Set $P'(x) = 0$:
$x = 30$, which is inside the domain.
$P''(x) = -6 < 0$, so $x = 30$ gives a maximum.
$P(30) = 5400 - 2700 = 2700$
Endpoints:
$P(0) = 0$
$P(50) = 9000 - 7500 = 1500$
The profit is greatest when $30$ items are sold.

questions.question_text:
The cost of running a machine for $x$ hours is $C(x) = 2x^{2} - 24x + 150$ dollars, for $0 \le x \le 10$.
Find the minimum cost.

options.why: Compared only the two endpoints and took the smaller of those.
Assumed the cost is least at the start of the domain, without differentiating.

questions.solution_text:
$C'(x) = 4x - 24$
Set $C'(x) = 0$:
$x = 6$, which is inside the domain.
$C''(x) = 4 > 0$, so $x = 6$ gives a minimum.
$C(6) = 72 - 144 + 150 = 78$
Endpoints:
$C(0) = 150$
$C(10) = 200 - 240 + 150 = 110$
The minimum cost is $\$78$.

questions.question_text:
A boat travels $120$ km at a constant speed of $v$ km/h.
Its running cost is $\left(20 + \dfrac{v^{2}}{20}\right)$ dollars per hour, for $10 \le v \le 40$.
Find the speed that minimises the cost of the trip.

options.why: Assumed the fastest allowed speed is always cheapest, ignoring the rising hourly running cost.
Assumed the slowest allowed speed is cheapest, ignoring the extra hours it takes.

questions.solution_text:
Time for the trip $= \dfrac{120}{v}$ hours.
$C = \left(20 + \dfrac{v^{2}}{20}\right)\left(\dfrac{120}{v}\right)$
$= \dfrac{2400}{v} + 6v$
$C'(v) = -\dfrac{2400}{v^{2}} + 6$
Set $C'(v) = 0$:
$v^{2} = 400$
$v = 20$, which is inside the domain.
$C''(v) = \dfrac{4800}{v^{3}} > 0$ for $v > 0$, so $v = 20$ gives a minimum.
$C(20) = 120 + 120 = 240$
Endpoints:
$C(10) = 240 + 60 = 300$
$C(40) = 60 + 240 = 300$
The cost is least at $20$ km/h.

questions.question_text:
A rectangular garden bed has an existing wall along one side and $56$ metres of fencing for the other three sides.
Let $x$ metres be the length of each side perpendicular to the wall.
What value of $x$ maximises the area?

options.why: Differentiated $2x^{2}$ as $2x$ and solved $56 - 2x = 0$ instead of $56 - 4x = 0$.
Divided the correct equation $4x = 56$ by $8$ instead of $4$.

questions.solution_text:
The side parallel to the wall has length $56 - 2x$ metres.
$A(x) = x(56 - 2x) = 56x - 2x^{2}$, for $0 < x < 28$.
$A'(x) = 56 - 4x$
Set $A'(x) = 0$:
$x = 14$, which is inside the domain.
$A''(x) = -4 < 0$, so $x = 14$ gives a maximum.
$A(14) = 784 - 392 = 392$
As $x$ approaches either $0$ or $28$, the area approaches $0$.
The area is greatest when $x = 14$ metres.

questions.question_text:
A manufacturer's profit is $P(x) = \dfrac{x^{3}}{3} - 7x^{2} + 40x$ thousand dollars, where $x$ is the number of units sold in thousands, for $2 \le x \le 12$.
How many units should be sold to maximise the profit?

options.why: Selected the stationary point $x = 10$, which is a local minimum, instead of comparing candidate profit values.
Selected the largest allowed production quantity without comparing its profit with the stationary values.
Found $x = 4$ but did not convert the quantity from thousands of units.

questions.solution_text:
$P'(x) = x^{2} - 14x + 40 = (x - 4)(x - 10)$
Set $P'(x) = 0$:
$x = 4$ or $x = 10$, both inside the domain.
$P''(x) = 2x - 14$
$P''(4) = -6 < 0$, so $x = 4$ is a local maximum.
$P''(10) = 6 > 0$, so $x = 10$ is a local minimum.
$P(4) = \dfrac{64}{3} - 112 + 160 = \dfrac{208}{3}$
$P(10) = \dfrac{1000}{3} - 700 + 400 = \dfrac{100}{3}$
Endpoints:
$P(2) = \dfrac{8}{3} - 28 + 80 = \dfrac{164}{3}$
$P(12) = 576 - 1008 + 480 = 48$
The largest value is $\dfrac{208}{3}$, at $x = 4$.
The profit is greatest when $4000$ units are sold.

questions.question_text:
The height of a drone above the ground is $h(t) = t^{3} - 12t^{2} + 36t + 10$ metres, for $0 \le t \le 9$ seconds.
Find the greatest height it reaches.

options.why: Stopped at the local maximum inside the domain without checking the endpoint values.
Gave the starting height $h(0)$ rather than the largest value on the domain.

questions.question_text:
A factory's weekly profit is $P(x) = 140x - 2x^{2}$ hundreds of dollars, where $x$ is the number of machines running, for $0 \le x \le 60$.
Find the maximum weekly profit in dollars.

options.why: Left the answer in hundreds of dollars instead of converting to dollars.
Multiplied by $10$ rather than $100$ when converting hundreds of dollars to dollars.
Multiplied the optimising value $x = 35$ by $100$ instead of evaluating $P(35)$.

questions.solution_text:
$P'(x) = 140 - 4x$
Set $P'(x) = 0$:
$x = 35$, which is inside the domain.
$P''(x) = -4 < 0$, so $x = 35$ gives a maximum.
$P(35) = 4900 - 2450 = 2450$
Endpoints:
$P(0) = 0$
$P(60) = 8400 - 7200 = 1200$
The greatest value is $2450$ hundreds of dollars, so the maximum weekly profit is $\$245\,000$.

questions.question_text:
A line through $P(3,4)$ meets the positive axes at $X(x,0)$ and $Y(0,y)$, where $x > 3$.
Given that $y = \dfrac{4x}{x - 3}$, find the minimum area of triangle $XOY$, where $O$ is the origin.

options.why: Gave the optimising intercept $x = 6$ instead of evaluating the area.
Used $xy$ instead of $\dfrac{1}{2}xy$ for the triangle's area at $x = 6$ and $y = 8$.
Evaluated the area at the stationary root $x = 0$, which lies outside the domain $x > 3$.

questions.solution_text:
$A(x) = \dfrac{1}{2}xy = \dfrac{2x^{2}}{x - 3}$, for $x > 3$.
Using the quotient rule:
$A'(x) = \dfrac{4x(x - 3) - 2x^{2}}{(x - 3)^{2}} = \dfrac{2x(x - 6)}{(x - 3)^{2}}$
Set $A'(x) = 0$:
$x = 0$ or $x = 6$.
Only $x = 6$ is in the domain.
For $3 < x < 6$, $A'(x) < 0$; for $x > 6$, $A'(x) > 0$.
The area decreases then increases, so $x = 6$ gives a global minimum.
As $x \to 3^{+}$ or $x \to \infty$, $A(x) \to \infty$.
$A(6) = \dfrac{2(36)}{3} = 24$
The minimum area is $24$ square units.

questions.question_text:
A courier van covers $300$ km at a constant speed of $v$ km/h.
Wages cost $\$45$ per hour and fuel costs $\dfrac{v^{2}}{80}$ dollars per hour, for $30 \le v \le 110$.
Find the minimum total cost of the trip, to the nearest dollar.

options.why: Took the fastest allowed speed, assuming less time on the road always costs less.
Took the slowest allowed speed, assuming less fuel per hour always costs less.
Used only the wages term $\dfrac{13\,500}{v}$ at $v = 60$ and omitted the fuel cost.

questions.solution_text:
Time for the trip $= \dfrac{300}{v}$ hours.
$C = \left(45 + \dfrac{v^{2}}{80}\right)\left(\dfrac{300}{v}\right)$
$= \dfrac{13\,500}{v} + \dfrac{15v}{4}$
$C'(v) = -\dfrac{13\,500}{v^{2}} + \dfrac{15}{4}$
Set $C'(v) = 0$:
$v^{2} = \dfrac{4 \times 13\,500}{15} = 3600$
$v = 60$, which is inside the domain.
$C''(v) = \dfrac{27\,000}{v^{3}} > 0$ for $v > 0$, so $v = 60$ gives a minimum.
$C(60) = 225 + 225 = 450$
Endpoints:
$C(30) = 450 + 112.5 = 562.5$
$C(110) \approx 122.73 + 412.5 = 535.23$
The minimum total cost is $\$450$.
